title: Diwali Couple Portrait Edit in Coordinated Festive Outfits
prompt:
Edit the photo I uploaded of two adults into a Diwali evening couple portrait. Keep both faces exactly as they are: same features, skin tones, expressions, hairstyles and body shapes. Both people must stay adults and look like themselves.

Outfits: coordinated but not identical festive wear in deep maroon and antique gold. One in a silk saree or lehenga with a fine zari border, the other in a bandhgala or kurta with a contrasting stole. Simple gold-tone jewellery, no oversized pieces.

Setting: the doorway of a home decorated for Diwali, with a marigold and mango-leaf toran above the door, a small rangoli at the threshold and a row of clay diyas along the step. Soft string lights on the wall behind.

Pose: standing side by side, relaxed and natural, one person lightly holding a lit diya at chest height.

Lighting and camera: warm diya and string-light glow as the main light, a soft blue dusk sky visible at the edge of the frame, shallow depth of field like a 50mm lens at f/2, sharp focus on both faces.

Format: vertical 4:5, natural colours, realistic photo style, no text, no watermark, no logos. Avoid plastic skin, extra fingers, altered faces and over-smoothing.

title: Bhai Dooj Tilak Portrait of Adult Siblings
prompt:
Turn my uploaded photo of two adult siblings into a warm Bhai Dooj portrait. Keep both faces exactly as they are, with real features, skin texture and expressions. Both people are adults and must stay recognisable.

Moment: one sibling is applying a red tilak with rice grains on the other's forehead using a ring finger. The other sits on a low wooden stool, smiling. A brass puja thali sits between them with a small lit diya, roli, rice, a few sweets and a coconut.

Clothing: festive cotton or silk ethnic wear in soft pastels or jewel tones, nothing flashy.

Setting: a sunlit room of an Indian home in the morning, with a marigold garland on a window frame and a few diyas from Diwali still on the sill. Background softly out of focus.

Lighting and camera: soft window light from one side, gentle warm fill from the diya, 35mm documentary look at eye level, crisp focus on the hands and faces.

Format: 4:5 vertical, realistic, candid feel, no text, no logos, no watermark. Avoid changing ages, faces or body shapes, and avoid extra hands or fingers.

title: Chhath Puja Sunset Ghat Greeting Card
prompt:
Create a Chhath Puja greeting card image for the Sandhya Arghya evening.

Scene: a wide river ghat at sunset. The sun is a large orange disc low over calm water. Devotees stand waist-deep in the river as small distant silhouettes, holding bamboo soups (winnowing baskets) piled with fruit, thekua and sugarcane, offering arghya towards the sun. Tall sugarcane stalks are tied into small canopies along the bank, with clay diyas lit at their base. Faint reflections ripple on the water.

Mood and style: peaceful, devotional, golden-hour painting style with soft brush texture and gentle haze. Warm orange, saffron and gold against a pale violet sky.

Text: leave the top third of the image as clean sky so I can add my own greeting. Do not render any text yourself.

Format: 4:5 vertical for WhatsApp and Instagram, plus a 16:9 version if possible. No logos, no watermark. Keep people small and non-identifiable silhouettes; no close-up faces.

title: Govardhan Puja Annakut Thali Greeting Card
prompt:
Design a Govardhan Puja greeting card centred on an Annakut food offering.

Subject: a small hill-shaped mound built from cooked rice and decorated on its sides with rows of colourful festival dishes in small brass and clay bowls: seasonal vegetables, kadhi, puris, sweets like laddoos and pedas, and fresh fruit. Tiny clay diyas and marigold petals ring the base. A few tulsi leaves rest on top.

Composition: three-quarter overhead view on a red cloth with a gold border, set on a wooden floor. Plenty of rich detail in the centre, calm space at the top for a greeting.

Lighting: warm, soft light from the diyas and a window, gentle shadows, appetising food-photo look.

Text: do not add any text; keep the top 25% uncluttered for my own message.

Format: 1:1 square and 9:16 story versions. Realistic food photography style, no people, no logos, no watermark. Avoid plastic-looking food and duplicated bowls.

title: Sharad Purnima Moonlit Kheer Greeting Card
prompt:
Create a greeting card image for Sharad Purnima night.

Scene: a rooftop terrace at night under a huge, bright full moon. In the foreground, a silver or brass bowl of rice kheer garnished with saffron strands, sliced almonds and pistachios sits on a low wooden stool, covered partly with a thin muslin cloth, left out in the moonlight as per tradition. Beside it, a small clay diya and a few white flowers (jasmine or parijat).

Background: soft silhouettes of nearby rooftops and a neem tree, a clear deep-blue sky with a few thin clouds lit silver by the moon.

Lighting: cool silver moonlight as the key light on the kheer, warm small glow from the diya for contrast. Calm, quiet mood.

Text: leave clean sky space in the upper third for my own greeting; do not render text.

Format: 4:5 vertical, photoreal with a slightly dreamy finish, no people, no logos, no watermark.

title: Karwa Chauth Mehndi Design on Hands, Flat-Lay Photo
prompt:
Generate a close-up photo of a fresh Karwa Chauth mehndi design on a pair of adult hands, for design inspiration.

Design: dark reddish-brown henna covering the palms and fingers. Centre of each palm: a round moon motif with a small sieve (channi) pattern and a karwa (clay pot) beside it. Around it: fine paisleys, lotus petals, net fills and thin vines that run up each finger, ending in solid fingertip caps. Keep lines crisp and symmetrical between both hands.

Styling: hands held palms-up, side by side, over a red silk dupatta with a gold border. A few red and gold glass bangles on the wrists. A small lit diya and a karwa pot slightly out of focus at the edge of the frame.

Lighting and camera: soft daylight from above, overhead flat-lay angle, macro-level detail on the henna lines.

Format: 4:5 vertical, realistic, only hands visible (no face), no text, no logos, no watermark. Avoid extra or merged fingers and smudged lines.

title: Diwali Sky Lantern Street at Night Phone Wallpaper
prompt:
Create a phone wallpaper of a narrow old-city street on Diwali night.

Scene: looking up a lane between two-storey houses with wooden balconies. Dozens of handmade paper sky lanterns (akash kandil) in star, hexagon and cylinder shapes hang from balconies and strings across the lane, glowing orange, magenta, teal and yellow. Rows of diyas line the balcony railings. A soft trail of firework sparks fades in the strip of sky above.

Mood and style: cinematic, rich and warm, gentle haze in the air, painterly realism, glowing paper texture visible on the lanterns.

Composition: vertical, lanterns dense at the top and middle, darker and simpler at the bottom third so app icons stay readable. No people in focus; a few soft distant figures at most.

Format: 9:19.5 phone ratio (or 9:16), high detail, no text, no logos, no watermark.

title: Diwali Mithai Box Packaging Design for a Local Sweet Shop
prompt:
Design Diwali gift-box packaging for a local sweet shop called [Shop name] in [City].

Box: a square rigid box for 500 g of assorted mithai with a lift-off lid. Show it closed (three-quarter view) and open (top view, showing laddoos, kaju katli and barfi in a gold-paper tray with eight compartments).

Artwork on the lid: deep maroon base with a repeating pattern of tiny diyas and marigold flowers in matte gold foil, a clean rounded label area in the centre for "[Shop name]" and a small line "Diwali Special". Sides: a thin border pattern inspired by a toran. Make the shop name and label text crisp and correctly spelled exactly as I typed it.

Presentation: product mock-up on a warm beige surface with two lit diyas and scattered petals, soft studio light, gentle shadow.

Output: one 4:5 image with both views side by side. No other brand logos, no barcodes, no prices, no claims like "best" or "No. 1". If my shop name is missing, use "[Shop name]" as visible placeholder text.

title: Diwali Gift Hamper Product Photo for an Online Store
prompt:
Create a clean product photo of a Diwali gift hamper for an online store listing.

Product: a woven basket or a kraft-paper box lined with red tissue, containing [list your items, e.g. dry-fruit jar, two scented candles, a small brass diya, a box of sweets, a greeting card]. Show only the items I list; do not add extras. Packaging should be plain or lightly patterned with no brand names.

Styling: hamper in the centre on a seamless warm-cream background, a satin ribbon in gold or maroon, two lit diyas and a few marigold petals around the base. Keep props minimal so the hamper is clearly the product.

Lighting and camera: soft studio light with a gentle warm accent from the diyas, three-quarter front angle at slight top-down view, everything sharp.

Output: two versions, 1:1 square (main listing image, clean background, no props outside the hamper) and 4:5 lifestyle (with diyas and petals). No text, no prices, no badges, no logos, no watermark. Avoid melted or duplicated items.

title: Diwali Room Decor Makeover From a Photo of Your Room
prompt:
Use the photo I uploaded of my room and redecorate it for Diwali. Keep the room's layout, walls, windows, doors, furniture positions and floor exactly as they are; only add decor and lighting.

Add:
- warm-white string lights along the top of the main wall or window
- a marigold and mango-leaf toran over the doorway
- a medium-sized rangoli near the entrance in red, yellow, white and green
- clay diyas in a row on a shelf or window sill and a few on the floor near the rangoli
- one or two brass urlis with floating flowers and candles
- cushion covers in maroon, mustard or emerald if there's a sofa

Keep it tasteful, not cluttered. Hide nothing important; do not cover switches or doors.

Lighting: evening, main lights dimmed, the room glowing from diyas and string lights, natural warm tones.

Output: same camera angle and aspect ratio as my photo, realistic interior-photo look, no people, no text, no logos. After the image, list the decor items you added in 5-8 short bullets so I can buy or make them.

title: Diwali Greeting Messages for Clients and Employees
prompt:
You are writing Diwali greetings for a business. Details:
- Business: [Business name], [what you do] in [City]
- Sender: [Name, role]
- Tone: [warm and professional / friendly and casual]
- Any real offer or event to mention: [e.g. office closed 8-9 Nov / none]

Write these, each in English and in simple Hindi (Devanagari):
1. A WhatsApp message to clients (40-60 words).
2. An email to clients: subject line plus a 90-130 word body that thanks them for the year without selling anything.
3. A message to employees (60-90 words) that mentions [any real holiday or bonus detail, or leave it out].
4. A LinkedIn post (80-120 words) with 2-3 relevant hashtags.
5. Three one-line greetings for a printed card or gift tag.

Rules: be inclusive (some readers may not celebrate Diwali; don't assume religion beyond the festival itself). Don't invent offers, discounts, numbers or achievements; if a detail is missing, write [VERIFY: detail]. No emojis in the email; at most two in WhatsApp. Avoid clichés like "May this Diwali bring" in more than one message.

Quality check at the end: list any [VERIFY] placeholders I need to fill.

title: Festive Sale Instagram Reel Script for a Local Shop
prompt:
Act as a short-video planner for a small Indian shop. Write a 20-30 second Instagram Reel script for our festive sale.

Shop details:
- Shop: [Shop name], [category e.g. sarees, electronics, home decor] in [Area, City]
- Real offer: [exact offer and dates, e.g. 15% off on kurtas, 1-10 Nov]
- Hero products: [2-3 products]
- How to buy: [walk-in / WhatsApp number / website]
- Language: [Hindi / Hinglish / English / regional]

Give me:
1. Hook (first 2 seconds): three options, each under 8 words, shown as on-screen text ideas.
2. Shot list: 6-8 shots in a table with columns Shot, What to film on a phone, Duration (s), On-screen text, Voiceover line.
3. Trending-style audio direction: describe the mood and beat (don't name copyrighted songs).
4. Caption (under 60 words) with a clear call to action and 5 relevant hashtags, including one local hashtag.
5. A 3-frame Story version.

Rules: use only the offer I gave; never invent discounts, stock levels, deadlines or customer quotes. Mark any missing detail [VERIFY]. Every shot must be filmable by one person with a phone in the shop.

title: Bollywood Retro Saree Portrait Photo Edit, 1960s Studio Look
prompt:
Restyle my uploaded picture as a portrait from a 1960s Hindi-film studio. My facial identity must not change at all: identical eyes, nose, lips, jawline, complexion and expression. I am an adult and the result must resemble me, never any actor.

Styling: a sheer chiffon saree in a solid colour (choose from mustard, coral or emerald) with a thin satin border, a fitted short-sleeve blouse, a voluminous bouffant hairstyle with a side part, winged eyeliner and a small bindi. Simple pearl studs. For a male subject, swap this for a slim-fit suit, thin tie and a neat side-parted pompadour.

Setting: a painted studio backdrop of a garden at golden hour, slightly soft, like an old film set.

Lighting and finish: warm golden key light from the side, soft glow on the skin, gentle film grain, slightly faded Technicolor tones, subtle vignette.

Output: a 4:5 portrait-orientation image without any lettering, poster titles, logos or watermark. Skip heavy beauty filters, keep hands natural with five fingers, and leave my features untouched.

title: Halloween 90s Bedroom Disposable-Camera Flash Photo Edit
prompt:
Edit my uploaded photo into a nostalgic Halloween snapshot that looks like it was shot on a cheap disposable camera in the late 1990s. Keep my face exactly as it is, same features and expression. The person must be an adult.

Costume cue: keep it small and homemade, e.g. paper cat ears, plastic vampire fangs, a drawn-on skull face-paint detail on one cheek, or a cardboard witch hat. Choose one that suits my photo.

Setting: a slightly messy bedroom at night: a carved pumpkin with a candle on the desk, a bowl of wrapped sweets, a CRT TV glowing in the corner, fairy lights and a paper bat garland on the wall.

Camera look: harsh direct on-camera flash, bright subject and quickly falling-off dark background, slight red-eye is fine, mild motion blur, warm-green colour cast, visible film grain, slightly soft focus, a tiny light leak in one corner.

Format: 4:5 or 3:2, no date stamp, no text, no logos, no watermark. Avoid gore, horror masks over the face and anything that changes my face.

title: Y2K Camcorder Still Photo Edit With Timestamp
prompt:
Turn my uploaded photo into a frame grabbed from an early-2000s home camcorder tape. Keep my face, body and pose exactly as they are; the person must be an adult.

Look:
- 4:3 frame with soft standard-definition sharpness
- slightly washed-out colours, lifted blacks, a little chroma bleed around bright edges
- faint horizontal scan lines and a light tracking wobble at the bottom edge
- auto-exposure feel: highlights a bit blown where the light hits

Overlay: a camcorder-style date and time in the bottom-right corner in a blocky orange-yellow digital font, showing [DD MM YYYY  HH:MM]. Add a small "REC" with a red dot at top-left. Spell these exactly as given.

Keep the original background but make it look like it was filmed on that device. No brand names on the overlay.

Format: 4:3, no other text, no logos, no watermark. Avoid changing my face and avoid heavy glitch that hides it.

title: Nano Banana 2.1 Bilingual Hindi-English Menu Board
prompt:
Design a chalkboard-style menu board for a small eatery, with every item in English and Hindi (Devanagari). Render all text exactly as written below and keep the Hindi spelling correct.

Eatery name (top, large): [Eatery name] / [नाम हिंदी में]
Section 1: "Chai & Coffee / चाय और कॉफ़ी"
- [Item 1 English] / [Item 1 Hindi] - Rs [price]
- [Item 2 English] / [Item 2 Hindi] - Rs [price]
Section 2: "Snacks / नाश्ता"
- [Item 3 English] / [Item 3 Hindi] - Rs [price]
- [Item 4 English] / [Item 4 Hindi] - Rs [price]
Footer: [Timings, e.g. 7 am - 10 pm]

Use only the items and prices I fill in; if a bracket is still empty, leave a blank line instead of inventing an item or price.

Style: black chalkboard with a natural wood frame, hand-lettered white chalk headings, small doodles of a kulhad, samosa and steam swirls in yellow and pink chalk. Clear hierarchy: name, sections, items, prices aligned on the right.

Format: 3:4 vertical at 2K, front view, flat and readable from a distance. No logos, no watermark, no extra text.

title: Nano Banana 2.1 Four-Character Comic Page With Consistent Faces
prompt:
I am uploading up to four reference images, one per character: [Character A], [Character B], [Character C], [Character D]. Use only images of yourself, of adults who agreed, or of original characters you own. Keep each character's face, hair, skin tone and outfit consistent in every panel.

Make a one-page, six-panel comic in a clean, colourful webcomic style.

Story: [one-line story, e.g. four friends try to cook a festival dinner and the power goes out].
Panels:
1. Wide establishing shot of all four in [location].
2-5. One panel focused on each character's reaction or action, following the story.
6. All four together for the punchline.

Speech bubbles: short lines (under 12 words) that I write here: [Panel 1 line], [Panel 2 line], [Panel 3 line], [Panel 4 line], [Panel 5 line], [Panel 6 line]. Render the text exactly; if a line is blank, leave that panel without a bubble.

Layout: 2 columns x 3 rows, white gutters, consistent lighting within the scene.

Format: 2:3 vertical at 2K. No logos, no watermark, no signature.

title: Claude Haiku 5.5: Bulk Product Catalogue Cleanup to JSON
prompt:
You are a catalogue-cleanup assistant processing products in bulk. I will paste rows of raw product data (titles, notes, specs, sometimes Hinglish) below. For each row, return one JSON object on its own line (JSON Lines), nothing else.

Fields:
- "sku": as given; if missing, null
- "title": clean title under 70 characters: brand (only if given) + product + key attribute + size/colour
- "category": one of [your category list, e.g. Sarees, Kurtas, Home Decor, Kitchen, Electronics]
- "attributes": object with only the attributes present in the input (material, colour, size, weight, pack_of)
- "bullets": 3 short benefit bullets, each under 15 words, based only on facts in the input
- "missing": list of important fields that the input lacks
- "flags": list of problems, e.g. "price missing", "conflicting sizes", "possible duplicate of <sku>"

Rules:
- Never invent specs, materials, prices, certifications or claims like "100% original". If unsure, put the field in "missing".
- Translate Hinglish or Hindi notes into plain English.
- Keep output valid JSON; escape quotes.

Input rows:
[paste rows here]

After the last line, output nothing else. I will spot-check 5 random rows against the input.

title: Flooded Room Surreal Interior Scene
prompt:
Create a surreal, quiet image of an ordinary living room that is partly flooded with still, crystal-clear water.

Scene: a mid-century living room with a sofa, a floor lamp, a wooden bookshelf and a framed painting. Calm water fills the room to knee height, perfectly still, reflecting everything above it like a mirror. A few objects float gently: an open paperback, a paper boat, a single orange leaf. Below the surface, the patterned rug and the legs of the furniture are visible, slightly distorted.

Light: soft late-afternoon sun through a tall window, casting rippled caustic patterns on the ceiling and walls. Dust in the light beams.

Mood and style: dreamlike but photoreal, muted teal and warm amber palette, film-like softness, 35mm wide-angle at eye level just above the waterline.

Format: 3:2 landscape (and a 4:5 crop if possible). No people, no text, no logos, no watermark. Avoid murky water, debris and anything that looks like a disaster scene.
